new_note: *And the nation also to whom they will be in bondage shall I judge, and after that they will come forth thence with much substance.* (Jubilees 14:14). *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* (Genesis 15:14). Jubilees carries the second half of the oath to Abram entire, not only the four hundred years of affliction but the judgment on the nation that afflicts and the coming out afterward with much in hand. Yahuah (God) told Abram the end before the bondage began; the exodus was promised in the same breath as the servitude. When Yashar'el (Israel) walked out of Egypt with the silver and gold of their neighbours, they were collecting on a word spoken to their father four centuries earlier.
member_note: Jubilees 14:14 — *after that they will come forth thence with much substance.* The exodus promised to Abram in the same breath as the bondage (Genesis 15:14).

new_note: *And they will all be called children of the living Elohim (God), and every angel and every spirit will know, yea, they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I love them.* (Jubilees 1:25). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). David says his members were written in the book before one of them existed. Jubilees puts that same foreknowledge at the scale of a people: before the gathering happens, Yahuah (God) already calls them My children, says he loves them, and promises that every angel and every spirit will come to know it. What is written in the book ahead of time is not only a body; it is a family. The children of the living Elohim (God) were his before they knew it, the way David's frame was known before it was formed.
member_note: Jubilees 1:25 — *they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness.* Known as his before they were, as David's members were written in the book before one of them was (Psalm 139:16).
flag: Old note described the divisions of days written in Jubilees 1:26-29, not 1:25; the Jubilees verse may be off. Rebuilt on 1:25 as given.

new_note: *And the judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tables in righteousness–even (the judgment of) all who depart from the path which is ordained for them to walk in; and if they walk not therein judgment is written down for every creature and for every kind.* (Jubilees 5:13). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). David knew a book in which things were written before they were. Jubilees shows another page of that same book: judgment ordained and written on the heavenly tables for every creature that leaves the path laid out for it. The path and the penalty were both written down ahead of time, not improvised after the fall. What the Watchers met at the flood was not a new decision; it was a line already written.
member_note: Jubilees 5:13 — *the judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tables in righteousness.* The same pre-written book David saw in Psalm 139:16, opened to the page of judgment.

new_note: *And he said: “Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the Elohim (God) of all;” and thus is it ordained concerning the two; and they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tables how Isaac blessed them.* (Jubilees 31:32). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). Isaac's blessing on Levi and Judah is not left to the wind; it is recorded on the heavenly tables as an eternal testimony. David looked into that same book and found his own members written there before any of them were. The book holds both: a man's frame before he is formed, and a father's blessing after it is spoken. Isaac can say "now I know that I have an eternal hope" because what is written in heaven does not fade with the voice that spoke it.
member_note: Jubilees 31:32 — *they record it as an eternal testimony to them on the heavenly tables how Isaac blessed them.* The blessing written in the same book where David's members were written (Psalm 139:16).

new_note: *And He finished speaking with him, and He went up from him, and Jacob looked till He had ascended into heaven.* (Jubilees 32:20). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). He finished speaking, went up, and Jacob watched until He had gone into heaven. What follows that ascent in Jubilees is the showing of all that would befall Jacob and his sons through the ages, which is the book David speaks of, where the days are written before one of them comes. The conversation ended on the ground at Bethel, but the record of Jacob's seed was already kept where He went up to. David's confidence and Jacob's upward gaze rest on the same thing: the days are written before they are lived.
member_note: Jubilees 32:20 — *He went up from him, and Jacob looked till He had ascended into heaven.* The One who spoke went up to where the days are written before they are (Psalm 139:16).
flag: Old note described the seven tablets showing Jacob all that would befall him and his sons, which is Jubilees 32:21, not 32:20; the Jubilees verse may be off by one. Rebuilt on 32:20 as given.

new_note: *And for this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tables as a law for the tithing again the tithe to eat before Yahuah (God) from year to year, in the place where it is chosen that His name should dwell, and to this law there is no limit of days for ever.* (Jubilees 32:10). *And thou shalt eat before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks; that thou mayest learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always.* (Deuteronomy 14:23). Moses' command to eat the tithe before Yahuah (God) in the place where he sets his name is not new at Sinai. Jubilees roots it in Jacob at Bethel tithing again the tithe, and says it is ordained on the heavenly tables with no limit of days. The place, the eating, and the name dwelling there are the same in both books. A law written in heaven before it was given through Moses is not one a later century can retire; Jubilees says plainly that it has no end of days.
member_note: Jubilees 32:10 — *in the place where it is chosen that His name should dwell, and to this law there is no limit.* The tithe law of Deuteronomy 14:23 was on the heavenly tables before Sinai, with no limit of days.

new_note: *For until that time there had not been revealed the ordinance and judgment and law in its completeness for all, but in your days (it has been revealed) as a law of seasons and of days, and an everlasting law for the everlasting generations.* (Jubilees 33:16). *Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.* (Psalm 139:16). The law against a son lying with his father's wife was always written; Jubilees says only that it had not yet been revealed in its completeness until the days of Moses, and then as an everlasting law for every generation. That is the order David describes: the thing stands in the book first, and the day it appears on earth comes afterward. Reuben was spared the full penalty not because the law did not exist but because it had not yet been shown. Revelation has a date; the writing does not.
member_note: Jubilees 33:16 — *there had not been revealed the ordinance and judgment and law in its completeness for all.* Written before it was revealed, the way David's days were written before they came (Psalm 139:16).

new_note: *And the land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, for Yahuah (God) was with him, and gave him favour and mercy for all his generations before all those who knew him and those who heard concerning him, and Pharaoh’s kingdom was well ordered, and there was no Satan and no evil person (therein).* (Jubilees 40:9). *He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:* (Psalm 105:21). The psalm says "He made him lord of his house," and the He is Yahuah (God), not Pharaoh. Jubilees reads the same way: Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, but the reason given is that Yahuah (God) was with him and gave him favour before everyone who knew him. Pharaoh signed, but the favour that put the ring on Joseph's hand came from elsewhere. A kingdom well ordered, with no Satan and no evil person in it, is what it looks like when Yahuah (God) is the one doing the appointing.
member_note: Jubilees 40:9 — *Yahuah (God) was with him, and gave him favour and mercy for all his generations.* Yahuah (God), not Pharaoh, made Joseph lord of the house (Psalm 105:21).
flag: Old note described Joseph being made ruler over all Egypt, which is Jubilees 40:7, not 40:9; the Jubilees verse may be off. Rebuilt on 40:9 as given.

new_note: *And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: “Seven years will come (in which there will be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.* (Jubilees 40:3). *And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;* (Genesis 41:30). Joseph's reading of the dreams stands word for word between the two books: seven years of plenty over all Egypt, then seven years of famine. Jubilees adds that the two dreams were one, and that the famine would be one such as had not been seen in the land; Genesis says the plenty will be forgotten and the famine will consume the land. It is the same interpreter speaking, and the interpretation came from Elohim (God), not from Joseph, which is why it came to pass exactly.
member_note: Jubilees 40:3 — *seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.* The same reading Joseph gives Pharaoh in Genesis 41:30.

new_note: *I shall go down with you, and I shall bring you up (again), and in this land will you be buried, and Joseph will put his hands upon your eyes. Fear not; go down into Egypt.”* (Jubilees 44:6). *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* (Genesis 15:14). When Jacob fears to go down to Egypt, the word he receives is the oath to his grandfather coming due. Abram was told his seed would serve a nation, that the nation would be judged, and that they would come out afterward with great wealth. "I shall go down with you, and I shall bring you up" is that promise in the first person, spoken to the man about to enter the bondage. Jacob's burial in Canaan and Joseph's hands on his eyes are the near end; the coming out with much is the far end, fixed before he ever went down.
member_note: Jubilees 44:6 — *I shall go down with you, and I shall bring you up (again).* The oath of Genesis 15:14, in and judged and out, spoken to Jacob at the door of Egypt.

new_note: *And He said “Your spirit will not always abide on man; for they also are flesh and their days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”* (Jubilees 5:8). *For thus says Yahuah (the Lord), Behold I give you a period of one hundred and twenty years; if you will turn to me and forsake your evil ways, then will I also turn away from the evil which I told you, and it shall not exist, says Yahuah (the Lord).* (Jasher 5:8). Both books put the same number on the same mercy. In Jubilees it is a limit set on flesh: the Spirit will not always abide on man, and a hundred and twenty years is the measure. Jasher hears it as a door left open: a period of a hundred and twenty years, and if you will turn to me the evil will not come. Genesis 6:3 carries the number; these two tell you it was a space for repentance before the flood, not merely a lifespan. The decree and the offer were the same hundred and twenty years.
member_note: Jubilees 5:8 — *Your spirit will not always abide on man; for they also are flesh.* The hundred and twenty years that Jasher 5:8 calls a space to turn before the flood.

new_note: *And Noah made the ark in all respects as He commanded him, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week in the fifth year (on the new moon of the first month).* (Jubilees 5:22). *And Noah rose up, and he made the ark, in the place where Elohim had commanded him, and Noah did as Elohim had ordered him.* (Jasher 5:33). Jasher says Noah rose up and made the ark where Elohim (God) commanded; Jubilees says he made it in all respects as He commanded, and gives the date. Obedience is the point in both. Jubilees adds the calendar, the twenty-seventh jubilee, fifth week, fifth year, on the new moon of the first month, because Jubilees counts everything by the reckoning of time Yahuah (God) gave. The ark was built on command, in the right place, and on a dated day.
member_note: Jubilees 5:22 — *Noah made the ark in all respects as He commanded him.* The obedient building Jasher 5:33 records, here given its date.

new_note: *And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.* (Jubilees 8:10). *And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.* (Jasher 7:1). Jasher names the three sons and says children were born to them after the flood; Jubilees picks up once those families have grown and shows the earth divided into three parts, one for each son, by inheritance. The division was not a scramble for land; one who had been sent, an angel, was present with them as they did it. The brothers of Jasher 7 become the heads of the three portions of the whole earth. What Jasher begins as a family list, Jubilees finishes as a map.
member_note: Jubilees 8:10 — *they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth.* The three sons Jasher 7:1 names become the three portions of the earth.

new_note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.* (Jasher 7:19). Both books explain the name the same way: Peleg means division, and he was named for what was happening in his days. Jasher says the sons of men were divided and in the latter days the earth was divided; Jubilees says the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves when he was born. The name is a date stamp. Eber named his son after a world event, and both books kept the reason.
member_note: Jubilees 8:8 — *for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves.* The same reason for the name that Jasher 7:19 gives.

new_note: *For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”* (Jubilees 10:19). *And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so.* (Jasher 7:42). Jasher gives the man: Nimrod, reigning after his heart's desire, advised by his counselors to build a city for his palace. Jubilees gives the place and the boast: they left Ararat eastward to Shinar and built the city and the tower to climb into heaven by it. Put together, the tower was a king's project with a king's ambition, not a village's. "In his days" in Jubilees is Nimrod's days, and Jasher tells you who he was.
member_note: Jubilees 10:19 — *in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”* The city Jasher 7:42 says Nimrod's counselors advised him to build.

new_note: *And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.* (Jubilees 9:3). *And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.* (Jasher 10:32). Jasher tells of Asshur son of Shem going out with a large company to a distant land, finding a wide valley, and building four cities named after themselves. Jubilees had already allotted him that ground: the second portion of Shem's share, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar to the border of India. Jasher's "distant land that they found" was not stumbled upon; it was his by lot. The walking and the allotment are the same inheritance seen from two sides.
member_note: Jubilees 9:3 — *for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar.* The land Jasher 10:32 says Asshur went out and built four cities in.

new_note: *And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.* (Jubilees 9:1). *And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.* (Jasher 10:19). Jasher names Ham's four sons; Jubilees shows Ham dividing his portion among those same four, laid out from east to west: Cush to the east, then Mizraim, then Put, then Canaan on the sea. One book is the roll call and the other is the map. Canaan's lot on the sea matters later, because Canaan did not keep to it but settled in Shem's portion, and the land that bears his name was never his by right.
member_note: Jubilees 9:1 — *Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east.* The four sons of Ham that Jasher 10:19 names, receiving their lots.

new_note: *And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.* (Jubilees 9:8). *And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.* (Jasher 10:7). Jasher lists Japheth's seven sons; Jubilees takes the first two of that list and places them on the ground, Gomer's portion east from the north side to the river Tina, Magog's the inner north as far as the sea of Meot. The same names, now with borders. The far north was Magog's lot from the division of the earth, which is worth remembering whenever the prophets speak of Magog and the north.
member_note: Jubilees 9:8 — *the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ.* The sons of Japheth Jasher 10:7 lists, Gomer and Magog, given their borders.

new_note: *For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.* (Jubilees 10:25). *And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.* (Jasher 10:2). Jasher opens with the result: the sons of men scattered for their sin at the tower into the four corners of the earth. Jubilees gives the means and the name: the language confounded at Shinar, so the place is called Babel, and from there they went out each to his own cities according to his language and his nation. Jasher's "many divisions" are Jubilees' languages. The scattering was judgment on the tower, and both books say so.
member_note: Jubilees 10:25 — *from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.* The scattering from the tower that Jasher 10:2 opens with.

new_note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.* (Jasher 10:1). Jasher 10 opens with Peleg's death in Abram's forty-eighth year, at two hundred and thirty-nine years old; Jubilees gives his birth and the reason for his name. The man whose name means division was born as the earth was being divided and died in the days of the man through whom it would be gathered into one seed. Two books tell the two ends of Peleg's life. The name given at his birth was the headline of his generation.
member_note: Jubilees 8:8 — *in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves.* The birth of the Peleg whose death Jasher 10:1 records.

new_note: *And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week that he spoke to his father, and informed him that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him.* (Jubilees 12:28). *And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and all the souls of his household and went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan. And when they came as far as the land of Haran they remained there, for it was exceedingly good land for pasture, and of sufficient extent for those who accompanied them.* (Jasher 13:1). Jasher tells how Terah brought the family out of Ur as far as Haran and stayed because the pasture was good. Jubilees picks up at the end of that stay: Abram speaks to his father and tells him he is going on to Canaan to see it. Haran was meant as a stop and became a settlement, so the call to Canaan had to be answered from inside a comfortable place. Both books keep the same road and the same halt on it.
member_note: Jubilees 12:28 — *he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him.* Leaving the Haran stop that Jasher 13:1 says Terah settled into.

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) said to him: “To you and to your seed will I give this land.”* (Jubilees 13:3). *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). At Abram's entry into Canaan both books have Yahuah (God) speak the same grant: this land to you and to your seed. Jasher expands it, forever, seed like the stars of heaven, all the lands you see; Jubilees gives it in one sentence. The land was given to a bloodline before that bloodline existed. Every later argument about who holds it begins at this word to Abram, not at any treaty.
member_note: Jubilees 13:3 — *“To you and to your seed will I give this land.”* The land grant at Abram's entry that Jasher 13:7 records.

new_note: *And in this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and departed and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar.* (Jubilees 16:10). *And at that time Abraham journeyed from the plain of Mamre, and he went to the land of the Philistines, and he dwelt in Gerar; it was in the twenty-fifth year of Abraham’s being in the land of Canaan, and the hundredth year of the life of Abraham, that he came to Gerar in the land of the Philistines.* (Jasher 20:1). Both books move Abraham from the plain of Mamre to Gerar at the same point in the story. Jubilees dates it by the month and places him between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar; Jasher dates it to his hundredth year, the twenty-fifth in Canaan, and names the land as the Philistines'. The year of Isaac's birth is the year of the move. Sarah will be taken by Abimelech there, and both books are setting the stage.
member_note: Jubilees 16:10 — *Abraham moved from Hebron, and departed and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur in the mountains of Gerar.* The move to Gerar that opens Jasher 20:1.

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for He had tried him through his country and with famine, and had tried him with the wealth of kings, and had tried him again through his wife, when she was torn (from him), and with circumcision, and had tried him through Ishmael and Hagar, his maid-servant, when he sent them away.* (Jubilees 17:17). *And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the word that Isaac spoke to Ishmael, and it seemed good in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he thought to try Abraham in this matter.* (Jasher 22:45). Jasher explains how the test of Isaac came about: Yahuah (the Lord) heard Isaac's word to Ishmael and thought to try Abraham in this matter. Jubilees lists the trials already behind him, his country, famine, the wealth of kings, his wife torn from him, circumcision, Ishmael and Hagar sent away, and says Yahuah (God) knew he was faithful. The test on the mountain was not to discover something unknown. It was the next in a series Abraham had already been passing, and the one who tried him knew him before he tried him.
member_note: Jubilees 17:17 — *Yahuah (God) knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions.* The trials already passed before the one Jasher 22:45 says Yahuah (the Lord) thought to try him with.

new_note: *And in the middle of the fifth month he moved from thence, and dwelt at the Well of the Oath.* (Jubilees 16:11). *And Abimelech took the seven ewe lambs which Abraham had given to him, for he had also given him cattle and herds in abundance, and Abimelech swore to Abraham concerning the well, therefore he called that well Beersheba, for there they both swore concerning it.* (Jasher 22:9). Jubilees calls the place by what happened there: the Well of the Oath. Jasher tells what the oath was, Abimelech swearing to Abraham over the well, the seven ewe lambs as witness, and the name Beersheba given because both swore. Jubilees dates Abraham's move there to the middle of the fifth month; Jasher explains why the well carried a name at all. Beersheba means a sworn well, and both books are leaning on the same story.
member_note: Jubilees 16:11 — *he moved from thence, and dwelt at the Well of the Oath.* Beersheba, named for the oath Jasher 22:9 records.

new_note: *And He said, “Take your beloved son whom you love, (even) Isaac, and go to the high country, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will point out to you.”* (Jubilees 18:2). *At that time the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came to Abraham, and he said to him, Abraham, and he said, Here I am.* (Jasher 23:1). Jasher gives the call: the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came, "Abraham," and he answered, "Here I am." Jubilees gives what the word said: take your beloved son, Isaac, go to the high country, and offer him on a mountain I will show you. One book has the summons and the other the command. "Here I am" was spoken before Abraham knew what was going to be asked, which is the whole shape of his faith.
member_note: Jubilees 18:2 — *Take your beloved son whom you love, (even) Isaac, and go to the high country.* The command that followed the "Here I am" of Jasher 23:1.

new_note: *And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron.* (Jubilees 19:2). *And at her bier was Shem, his sons Eber and Abimelech, together with Anar, Ashcol and Mamre, and all the grandees of the land followed her bier.* (Jasher 24:14). Jubilees records Sarah's death with its date, the first year of the third week of the jubilee, at Hebron. Jasher shows who came to her bier: Shem, with Eber and Abimelech, Anar, Ashcol and Mamre, and all the grandees of the land. Shem was still alive to bury Sarah; the generation of the ark and the generation of the promise overlapped. The woman through whom the seed came was followed to her grave by the man who came through the flood.
member_note: Jubilees 19:2 — *the days of the life of Sarah were accomplished, and she died in Hebron.* The death Jasher 24:14 says Shem and Eber followed to the bier.

new_note: *This is the tenth trial wherewith Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.* (Jubilees 19:8). *And the life of Sarah was one hundred and twenty-seven years, and Sarah died; and Abraham rose up from before his dead to seek a burial place to bury his wife Sarah; and he went and spoke to the children of Heth, the inhabitants of the land, saying,* (Jasher 24:1). Jasher tells it plainly: Sarah died at a hundred and twenty-seven, and Abraham rose up from before his dead to seek a burial place from the children of Heth. Jubilees counts that same errand as the tenth trial, and says he was found faithful and patient in spirit. Buying a grave in a land he had been promised and did not yet own, from the men who held it, without complaint, was a test, and Jubilees says he passed it. Faith is not only on the mountain with the knife; it is also in the field with the silver.
member_note: Jubilees 19:8 — *This is the tenth trial wherewith Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.* Burying Sarah (Jasher 24:1) counted as Abraham's tenth trial.

new_note: *And it came to pass in the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks–that is, the feast of the first-fruits of the harvest–to Abraham, their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come.* (Jubilees 22:1). *And all the inhabitants of the land of Haran, and all the families of the house of Abraham, and all the princes and grandees, and the sons of Abraham by the concubines, all came when they heard of Abraham’s death, and they requited Abraham’s kindness, and comforted Isaac his son, and they buried Abraham in the cave which he bought from Ephron the Hittite and his children, for the possession of a burial place.* (Jasher 26:31). Jubilees shows the last feast of weeks of Abraham's life, with Isaac and Ishmael both come to him from the Well of the Oath, and the old man glad to have his two sons together. Jasher shows the funeral: all Haran, all the house, the princes, and the sons of the concubines, burying him in the cave bought from Ephron. The feast and the burial sit in the same year. Both sons were at the table before they were at the grave, and Abraham died having kept the feast.
member_note: Jubilees 22:1 — *Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks.* The last feast of the year that Jasher 26:31 closes with Abraham's burial.

new_note: *And in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.* (Jubilees 19:13). *And after that came his brother, and his hand took hold of Esau’s heel, therefore they called his name Jacob.* (Jasher 26:15). Jasher gives the birth: the second came out with his hand on Esau's heel, so they called him Jacob. Jubilees gives the birth and then the men the two became, Jacob smooth and upright, dwelling in tents, Esau fierce and hairy, a man of the field. The division between the brothers began at the womb and showed in how they lived. Two sons of one mother, and only one of them called upright, and the book says so before the birthright is ever sold.
member_note: Jubilees 19:13 — *Rebecca bare to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau, and Jacob was a smooth and upright man.* The twins whose birth Jasher 26:15 records, already divided.

new_note: *And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.* (Jubilees 29:13). *And Esau hearkened to the voice of Jacob, and Esau returned with the four hundred men that were with him on their road to Seir, and Jacob and all belonging to him went that day as far as the extremity of the land of Canaan in its borders, and he remained there some time.* (Jasher 32:73). Jubilees dates the crossing of the Jabbok and puts the meeting with Esau on the same day: reconciled, and then parted, Esau to Seir and Jacob to his tents. Jasher tells the parting from the road: Esau heard Jacob's voice and turned back with his four hundred men toward Seir while Jacob went on to the edge of Canaan. Peace between the brothers did not make them one house. Esau went his way with his army and Jacob stayed a dweller in tents, and the two lines stayed two lines.
member_note: Jubilees 29:13 — *he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.* The parting Jasher 32:73 shows from the road, Esau back to Seir.

new_note: *And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed Yahuah (God).* (Jubilees 32:1). *At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.* (Jasher 36:1). Jasher records the command to go up to Bethel and build an altar to the One who delivered him; Jubilees records what happened the night Jacob was there: Levi dreamed he had been ordained priest of the Most High, he and his sons for ever, and woke and blessed Yahuah (God). The altar Jacob was sent to build needed a priesthood, and the priesthood was given at Bethel in a dream long before Sinai named Levi. Jasher gives the summons to Bethel and Jubilees gives what Bethel produced.
member_note: Jubilees 32:1 — *Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God).* The Bethel night that Jasher 36:1 sent Jacob to.

new_note: *And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, “The river of Deborah,” and the oak, “The oak of the mourning of Deborah.”* (Jubilees 32:30). *And the life of Rebecca was one hundred and thirty-three years, and she died and when Jacob heard that his mother Rebecca was dead he wept bitterly for his mother, and made a great mourning for her, and for Deborah her nurse beneath the oak, and he called the name of that place Allon-bachuth.* (Jasher 36:6). Both books bury Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, under an oak and name the place for the mourning. Jubilees dates it to the twenty-third of the month and gives the names, the river of Deborah and the oak of the mourning of Deborah; Jasher calls the oak Allon-bachuth and sets it beside Jacob's weeping for his mother Rebecca, dead at a hundred and thirty-three. A nurse received a named oak and a dated grave. The books remembered the servants, not only the patriarchs.
member_note: Jubilees 32:30 — *Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river.* The mourning oak Jasher 36:6 names Allon-bachuth.

new_note: *And Yahuah (God) appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him: “Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar’el (Israel) shall they name your name.”* (Jubilees 32:17). *And Jacob was a hundred years old when Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him, and blessed him and called his name Israel, and Rachel the wife of Jacob conceived in those days.* (Jasher 36:8). Jasher says Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob when he was a hundred years old, blessed him, and called his name Israel; Jubilees gives the words of the blessing: your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar'el (Israel) shall they name your name. The name was not won in the wrestling alone; it was spoken by Yahuah (God) at Bethel by night. A people carries that name because it was placed on one man by the mouth of the One who appeared to him.
member_note: Jubilees 32:17 — *“Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Yashar’el (Israel) shall they name your name.”* The renaming at Bethel that Jasher 36:8 records.

new_note: *And Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place, and he loved her.* (Jubilees 33:2). *And Reuben was jealous for his mother Leah on account of this, and he was filled with anger, and he rose up in his anger and went and entered the tent of Bilhah and he from there removed his father’s bed.* (Jasher 36:14). Jubilees shows the beginning: Reuben saw Bilhah bathing in a hidden place and wanted her. Jasher shows the motive and the deed: jealousy for his mother Leah, anger, and the removal of his father's bed from Bilhah's tent. One book gives the eye and the other the anger, and both end in the same sin against his father. Genesis 35:22 says it in a line; these two tell you how a firstborn lost his birthright.
member_note: Jubilees 33:2 — *Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, the concubine of his father, bathing in water in a secret place.* The sin Jasher 36:14 tells from the side of Reuben's anger.

new_note: *And these were the names of the sons of Jacob: the first-born Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Yahudah (Judah), Issachar, Zebulon, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali, and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob.* (Jubilees 33:22). *And these are the generations of Jacob who were born to him in Padan-aram, and the sons of Jacob were twelve.* (Jasher 36:16). Jasher says the sons of Jacob were twelve; Jubilees names them by their mothers, Leah's six, Rachel's two, Bilhah's two, Zilpah's two, and adds Dinah, the only daughter. The roster matters because the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) are these twelve men and no others, and the gathering of the scattered seed is a gathering of these names. Jasher gives the count and Jubilees gives the list.
member_note: Jubilees 33:22 — *these were the names of the sons of Jacob: the first-born Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Yahudah (Judah).* The twelve that Jasher 36:16 counts, here named by mother.
